sculpture.name: house model, model
sculpture.title: house model, model
sculpture.reason: This is a carved and painted house model in Northwest Coast style, with a raven figure over the doorway and a human-on-fish figure beneath — a classic Heiltsuk/Northwest Coast house-front crest design, consistent with the claimed culture.

sculpture.name: skulptur, figur, sculpture
sculpture.title: skulptur, figur, sculpture
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden zoomorphic figure (likely a whale or mask-top element), painted black, red, and white in Northwest Coast formline style, purchased in Victoria, BC with provenance attributed to Bella Bella (Heiltsuk) — consistent with Heiltsuk carving traditions of the region.

sculpture.name: staff
sculpture.title: staff
sculpture.reason: This is a carved and painted wooden speaker's staff with potlatch-ring hat figures, copper form, and crest imagery — a ceremonial regalia object consistent with Northwest Coast (Heiltsuk) traditional use, plausible for the claimed culture.

household.name: staff
household.title: staff
household.reason: A carved and painted wooden speaker's staff with Northwest Coast formline figures (killer whales, human/ancestor figures), attributed by the museum to Heiltsuk makers — a classic ceremonial/status object of this culture.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved and painted wooden transformation mask with a bird's head center flap and bear-depicting side flaps, explicitly attributed by the museum to Heiltsuk makers — a classic Northwest Coast ceremonial mask form consistent with this group.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: This is a classic Northwest Coast transformation/articulated-mouth face mask with formline painting, moving eyes, fur whiskers, and a movable cedar mandible — exactly the type of ceremonial mask made and used by Heiltsuk and related Northwest Coast peoples for winter ceremonial dances.

masks-ritual.name: mask, frontlet
masks-ritual.title: mask, frontlet
masks-ritual.reason: A carved and painted wooden frontlet with a bird (raven/hawk-like) face and human figure atop, in Northwest Coast style, worn as part of Heiltsuk ceremonial headdress regalia — matches the claimed culture and use.

jewelry.name: prydnad
jewelry.title: prydnad
jewelry.reason: The object is a labret (lip ornament) carved from horn, a known form of high-status women's adornment among the northern Northwest Coast peoples; the museum's own note names Heiltsuk among the groups who used this type, so it plausibly belongs to this culture even if indistinguishable from neighbours' examples.

jewelry.name: lip cleavage
jewelry.title: lip cleavage
jewelry.reason: This is a carved abalone shell lip/nose ornament, collected in British Columbia on the 1898 Alaska-Klondike expedition; such shell ornaments are typical of Northwest Coast groups including Heiltsuk, and nothing contradicts the attribution.
